problem: Acquiring users through paid advertising was expensive for a product people had to understand first.
title: Dropbox adds a two-sided referral program that rewards storage
context: Dropbox was an early-stage file-sync startup with about 100,000 registered users in September 2008.
decision_made: Give extra free storage to both the person who refers and the friend who joins.
action_taken: Modelled the programme on PayPal's signup bonus and ran it as a permanent part of the product.
observed_outcome: Founder Drew Houston's slides say the programme permanently raised signups by 60 percent, and registered users grew from 100,000 in September 2008 to 4 million in January 2010.
lessons: A reward that benefits both sides and gives something the company can afford can turn users into a growth channel.
limitations: Figures are from the founder's own 2010 slides, not an independent study. Other growth drivers, such as product quality, are not separated. A claim about 2 billion free storage was not found in the sources.

claims.claim_text: Dropbox created a two-sided referral programme that gave storage to both referrer and friend.
Houston's slides state that the programme permanently increased signups by 60 percent.
